description: We are Team Resplendant Zealot, and we are passionate about space exploration and programming. We have always been fascinated by the mysteries of outer space, and we enjoy learning Python and experimenting with what we can create using it. When we came across this challenge, we saw it as much more than just another project. It was an opportunity to combine our interests, strengthen our Python skills and experience how a hackathon works.
summary:
MISSION: BEYOND EARTH – THE ULTIMATE SPACE EXPLORER is an interactive 2D space exploration and survival game developed using Python and Pygame by Team Resplendant Zealot. Players can choose between the Moon and Mars, select one of four astronaut suits and customise a rover using five categories of components.
The main objective is to survive for 30 in-game days and establish a sustainable space base. Players explore the planetary environment, collect scientific samples, photograph locations, repair equipment and complete 15 scheduled missions. They must carefully manage six survival resources: oxygen, water, food, power, health and radiation.

The game includes 11 types of base facilities, an inventory and shop system, science quizzes every two days, random emergencies, changing weather and a day-and-night cycle. An ORBIT robot assistant provides survival warnings, emergency alerts, mission guidance and scientific facts.

Players begin with 1,000 credits and essential survival supplies, which they can use throughout their mission. The game also supports manual saving, automatic saving, continuing previous progress and sound settings.

To win, players must reach Day 30 and pass the final sustainability test by maintaining essential base facilities and minimum survival resource levels. The project combines space science, programming, strategic thinking and interactive gameplay to make learning about space more engaging and enjoyable.
details:
MISSION: BEYOND EARTH — Player Guide

1. What happens before starting the game?

The player goes through these screens in order:

1. Main Menu

  • New Game
  • Continue
  • How to Play
  • Settings
  • Quit

2. Planet Selection - 2 choices

  • The Moon
  • Mars

Each planet has different gravity, atmosphere, weather and radiation challenges.

3. Astronaut Suit Selection - 4 choices

  • Suit
  • Radiation Shield Suit
  • Thermal Protection Suit
  • Explorer Suit

Each suit has different radiation protection, temperature protection and efficiency.

4. Rover Customization

Build your rover by selecting its chassis, tyres, motor, camera and battery.

5. Space Journey

After building the rover, the game shows the space journey before entering planetary gameplay.

2. How many options can the player select?

  • Planet selection: 2 options.
  • Astronaut suit selection: 4 options.
  • Rover customization: 15 component choices across 5 categories.

Astronaut suits

Suit Main advantage

  • Basic Suit - Standard protection
  • Radiation Shield Suit - Better radiation protection
  • Thermal Protection Suit - Better temperature protection
  • Explorer Suit - Better efficiency and mobility

Rover customization

There are five categories, with three choices in each.

  • Chassis Light Frame, Heavy Frame, Modular Frame
  • Tyres Standard, All-Terrain, Reinforced
  • Motor Solar, Nuclear, Battery
  • Camera Basic, HD, 360°
  • Battery Small, Medium, Large

The rover screen also displays the selected components and performance specifications such as speed, durability, energy use, scan range and battery capacity.

3. How to play

  • Keyboard key Action : W / A / S / D - Move astronaut
  • Arrow keys Alternative movement : Shift + WASD Sprint
  • E - Interact
  • I - Open inventory
  • M - Open map / missions
  • Esc - Open/pause/menu

Using E: You can collect samples, photograph locations, repair buildings and enter or exit the rover when close enough to the object or rover.

4. Main objective of the game

Your mission is to survive 30 in-game days on the Moon or Mars and establish a sustainable space base.

You must maintain:

- Oxygen supply for breathing.

- Water supply for survival.

- Food production for the astronaut.

- Power generation for the base.

- Health and radiation safety.

- Working base equipment and life-support systems.

5. Missions in the game

Project contains 15 defined missions.

Day : Mission - What the player does

1 : Soil Sample - Collection Collect soil samples

2 : Rock Hunt - Collect rock samples

2 : Clean Solar Panels - Repair/maintain solar panels

3 : Explore New Area - Photograph a new area

4 : Repair Water Recycler - Repair the water recycler

5 : Oxygen Generator Maintenance - Maintain the oxygen generator

6 : Scientific Data Collection - Photograph a science location

7 : Start the Greenhouse - Build a greenhouse

8 : Photo Survey B - Photograph another survey location

10 : Deep Survey Mission - Complete a deep survey

12 : Emergency Equipment Repair - Repair multiple pieces of equipment

15 : Establish Research Lab - Build a research laboratory

18 : Establish Remote Outpost - Photograph the remote outpost location, 25–30 Final Sustainability Test - Survive until Day 30

The mission types include photography, collecting, repairing, building and survival. The mission schedule has some days without ordinary missions.

6. Resources you must manage

The game has six survival resources.

  • Oxygen - Needed for breathing
  • Water - Needed to survive
  • Food - Needed to maintain health
  • Power - Runs base equipment
  • Health - Represents astronaut condition
  • Radiation - Too much radiation damages health

The game shows resource levels using survival bars. You need to monitor them and use supplies or base facilities to restore them.

7. Base buildings

The player can establish and improve these base facilities:

- Astronaut Habitat

- Oxygen Generator

- Solar Panels

- Battery Storage

- Water Recycling Unit

- Resource Storage

- Greenhouse

- Medical Station

- Research Laboratory

- Radiation Shielding

- Rover Garage

8. Other game features

Science Quiz

A quiz appears every two in-game days. Each question has four answer choices and explains the correct science fact.

Emergency System

Random emergencies include water leakage, solar panel damage, oxygen generator failure, rover breakdown, dust storms, solar storms and habitat damage.

Inventory and Shop

Carry survival supplies and repair equipment. Earn credits from missions and quizzes, then purchase useful items.

ORBIT Robot Assistant

Provides resource warnings, emergency alerts, mission tips and space facts. The Robot Pet item is required for its tips.

Weather and Day/Night System

The game includes changing time, dust storms and solar storms that affect exploration and survival.

9. Starting items and credits

At the beginning of a new game, the astronaut receives:

- 2 Oxygen Tanks

- 3 Water Bottles

- 3 Food Packs

- 2 Repair Kits

- 1 Medkit

The game starts with 1,000 credits, which can be used in the shop.

10. How can the player win?

The final objective is to reach Day 30 and pass the sustainability test.

The following conditions must be satisfied:

  1. Astronaut Habitat must be active.
  2. Oxygen Generator must be active.
  3. Solar Panels must be active.
  4. Water Recycler must be active.
  5. Oxygen must be at least 40.
  6. Water must be at least 40.
  7. Food must be at least 20.
  8. Health must be at least 20.

If these conditions are met, the player can achieve the Victory Screen. Reaching Day 30 without meeting them does not count as a victory.

11. Save, continue and settings

- Continue: Load the previously saved game.

- Auto-save: The project includes saving at the end of an in-game day.

- Manual Save: Available through the pause menu.

- Settings: Toggle music and sound effects ON or OFF.

- Pause Menu: Open using ESC.
